PullRequest.Title: Modern UI: fade frosted glass menu background on close
PullRequest.Body:
🤖 Opened by an agent (Copilot), for review by @sbatten.

Fixes #343443

### Problem
The activity bar **Manage** (gear) context menu flickers when it closes (Windows 11, 1.141–1.143). Frames from the reporter's video show the item text fading out right away, while an empty panel stays on screen for a few more frames and then disappears suddenly.

### Cause
With Modern UI frosted glass and motion, which are both on by default on desktop, a menu has two layers:
- the glass panel: the container's `::before`, with tint and `backdrop-filter`
- the contents: `> .monaco-scrollable-element`

When the menu closes:
- the contents run `context-view-menu-motion-close` (opacity 1 → 0 plus scale)
- the glass `::before` runs `frosted-glass-menu-motion-close`, which only animated `transform`

So the glass stayed fully opaque for the whole 150ms close and was then hidden all at once. This came in with b0a5501f5fe.

### Fix
- **`menu.ts`:** `frosted-glass-menu-motion-close` now also animates `opacity`, from the same captured start opacity (`--vscode-context-view-menu-motion-close-start-opacity`, default 1) to 0, with the same duration and easing as the contents. The opacity is on the `::before` that owns the `backdrop-filter`, not on an ancestor, so the blur still renders while the panel fades.
- **`contextview.ts`:** export the existing close-start-opacity variable constant so `menu.ts` can use it.
- **`frostedGlass.test.ts`:** the closing-motion test used to assert `paintOpacity: '1'`. It now checks that at 75ms the glass and contents have the same opacity (below 1), and that at 145ms the glass is close to 0. It covers ordinary and shadow-root menus, in editor and Agents windows.
- **Modern UI README:** updated to describe the new closing behavior.

Unchanged:
- opening motion (scale only)
- submenus
- reduced motion (dismisses immediately)
- high-contrast, non-glass and legacy menus
- action-widget pickers

### How it was tested
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/frostedGlass.test.ts --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/menu/menu.test.ts --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/contextview/contextview.test.ts --browser chromium`: passed, 87 passing.
- With only the keyframe change reverted, `frostedGlass.test.ts`: 4 failing (`fadesTogether` and `glassGoneNearEnd` are false), as expected.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed .ts files>`: passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- Code OSS on macOS, with `window.menuStyle: custom` (the HTML menu Windows uses): opened Manage, pressed Escape, paused the close animations at 0/15/30/60/90/120ms, and read computed opacities.
  - Before the fix: the glass stays at 1.00 while the items go 0.60 → 0.33 → 0.08 → 0.02 → 0.00.
  - After the fix: glass and items match at every sample and are both 0 by 120ms.
- Captures over editor text, compared with a no-blur reference, show the blur still renders during the fade.
- Not tested on Windows itself.

To try it: with the default Modern UI and frosted glass settings on desktop, open the gear menu and press Escape. The panel and items should fade out together, with no empty panel left behind.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close a top-level frosted-glass context menu or dropdown with motion enabled, including activity-bar Manage, title-bar overflow, extensions/MCP/plugin actions, and agent-session menus.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Calling ContextView.hide synchronously captures the current content opacity/transform, adds the closing class, and starts the existing 150 ms close interval. The changed CSS interpolates opacity on the same ::before glass layer that already interpolates transform and owns backdrop-filter; disposal and DOM hiding occur after the existing timeout. The animation is visual and does not add work that must complete before command execution or other workflow progress.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the pixel area of the single visible menu and the fixed number of animation frames, not the number of menu actions, repositories, messages, or lifetime. Effective animated-target cardinality remains two: content and glass.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A context view owns one active top-level menu; its content animation and ::before glass animation run in parallel. The changed selector excludes nested .monaco-submenu elements. Repeated hide calls are coalesced by hidingContextView, and skipAnimation completes the pending hide instead of starting another animation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or cache key participates. Cold and warm closes use the same stylesheet and bounded animation; the stylesheet and menu rules already existed before the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff adds one opacity interpolation to an already transformed backdrop-filter pseudo-element for one bounded 150 ms close, while existing lifecycle code removes the class and CSS variables and hides the view at completion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Opacity compositing cost can vary by menu pixel area, Chromium implementation, and GPU/driver, but the diff does not add another backdrop-filter, extend the duration, increase menu cardinality, or introduce per-item work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The incremental compositor property is bounded to the existing close animation, adds no synchronous geometry read beyond the pre-existing close preparation, and introduces no boundary calls, fan-out, retained state, or longer critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dismiss menus with reduced motion, without frosted glass, in high contrast, or dismiss nested submenus.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: These variants do not match the new frostedGlassMotionMenuSelector: motion eligibility requires modern-ui-frosted-glass plus monaco-enable-motion, glass CSS excludes high-contrast modes, and the selector excludes .monaco-submenu. Immediate dismissal therefore remains on the pre-existing hide path and is off the changed animation path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: No changed work regardless of menu size or dismissal frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new animation runs in these variants; dismissal remains immediate or follows unchanged non-glass behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved, and eligibility is determined by existing ancestor classes and CSS selectors on every close.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the selector and ContextView.hide eligibility checks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for PR causality because the added keyframe declarations are unreachable in these variants.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change: the diff is gated away from reduced-motion, non-glass, high-contrast, and submenu paths.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and every diff hunk. Traced menu-close eligibility, interruption, cleanup, ordinary and shadow-root rendering, caller coverage, reduced-motion gating, and compositor/backdrop behavior. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue or qualifying regression fix was found.
